claims.claim_text: The indexed Jack Brown is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private identifier and exact indexed name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated November 30, 1942; the index documents an OSS personnel file but not the OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The Milwaukee diving-equipment designer Jack Browne differs in surname spelling and wartime chronology; other common-name candidates lacked the private identifier or Box 84 linkage.

claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private identifier and indexed name.

claims.match_notes: No employer, warehouse, store, product, worksite, exact title, or immediate OSS predecessor is inferred from the category.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked index supplies Howard Brown, a private identifier, and Box 84 but no rank, middle initial, occupation, or other public discriminator. The official Army merged file supplied no exact record; because that file has documented omissions and excludes officers, absence is not treated as disproof. A Signal Corps officer namesake could not be linked to the indexed identifier or file.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 84 for full name, rank, branch, residence, occupation, employer, and service chronology; test any recovered details against Signal Corps and other official military records.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked OSS index and official Army merged file agree on Jack Brown's exact indexed name and private identifier. The identifier remains withheld; the Army row dates entry to November 30, 1942 and carries civilian occupation code 788.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 84 for the warehousing or storekeeping employer and Army-to-OSS chronology.

research_attempts.query_text: Howard Brown: visually checked NARA index and private identifier; official Army bulk comparison; CIA, OSS, Signal Corps, employment, occupation, institutional, newspaper, obituary, directory, and archival searches.
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: The official Army merged file supplied no exact row. A lieutenant in the 2nd Signal Service Company and other same-name candidates lacked the indexed private identifier or Box 84 linkage.
research_attempts.research_notes: Bulk-file absence is not disproof because the series has omissions and excludes officers. No identity or employer was established.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 84 and test recovered details against official Signal Corps and military records.
